source: Easton's Bible Dictionary (M.G. Easton, 1897, Public Domain)
note: 전체 약 4,000개 항목 목표 중 A자(99개, id1-99) + B자(295개, id100-394) + C자(278개, id395-672) 수집 완료. 항목은 요약(축약) 방식. 다음 세션 D자부터 이어서 추가 예정.

entries.definition: Alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet, as Omega is the last. These letters occur in the text of Rev. 1:8,11; 21:6; 22:13, and are represented by "Alpha" and "Omega" respectively (omitted in R.V., 1:11). They mean "the first and last." (Comp. Heb. 12:2; Isa. 41:4; 44:6; Rev. 1:11,17; 2:8.) In the symbols of the early Christian Church these two letters are frequently combined with the cross or with Christ's monogram to denote his divinity.
entries.definition_ko: 알파, 헬라어 알파벳의 첫 글자(오메가가 마지막 글자). 계 1:8,11; 21:6; 22:13에 등장하며 "알파"와 "오메가"로 각각 표현된다(1:11에서는 R.V.에서 생략). "처음과 마지막"을 뜻한다(비교. 히 12:2; 사 41:4; 44:6; 계 1:11,17; 2:8). 초대 교회의 상징에서 이 두 글자는 흔히 십자가나 그리스도의 모노그램과 결합되어 그의 신성을 나타냈다.

entries.definition: the eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.
entries.definition_ko: 아므람과 레위의 딸 요게벳의 맏아들(출 6:20). 어떤 이들은 이름의 뜻을 "산악인"으로, 다른 이들은 "능력의 산" 또는 "빛을 비추는 자"로 설명한다. 그는 모세보다 3년 먼저, 그리고 누이 미리암보다는 여러 해 후에 애굽에서 태어났다(출 2:1,4; 7:7). 유다 지파 암미나답의 딸 엘리세바를 아내로 맞아(출 6:23; 대상 2:10) 나답과 아비후, 엘르아살과 이다말 네 아들을 낳았다. 이스라엘이 애굽에서 나올 때가 가까워지자 그는 하나님의 보내심을 받아(출 4:14,27-30) 오래 떨어져 있던 형제 모세를 만나 출애굽의 모든 일에서 그와 협력하게 되었다. 그는 모세의 "입" 곧 대언자가 되어야 했으니, 말이 유창했기 때문이다(출 7:1,2,9,10,19). 그는 맡겨진 일에 신실했고 바로와의 모든 만남에서 모세 곁을 지켰다. 르비딤에서 아말렉과 첫 전투를 벌일 때, 모세가 언덕 위에서 하나님의 지팡이를 든 손을 펼치고 있었는데, 이때 아론과 훌이 그의 손을 붙들어 여호수아와 이스라엘 용사들이 승리를 얻었다(출 17:8-13). 그 후 시내산 앞에 진을 쳤을 때, 모세가 율법의 돌판을 받으러 산에 올라갈 때 아론과 두 아들 나답과 아비후는 이스라엘 장로 칠십 인과 함께 산 중턱까지 동행하며 멀리서 하나님의 영광을 보았다(출 19:24; 24:9-11). 모세가 산에 머무는 동안 아론은 백성에게 돌아와, 두려움이나 지도력 부족, 성품의 흔들림으로 인해 그들의 요구에 굴복하여 금송아지를 만들고 예배의 대상으로 세웠다(출 32:4; 시 106:19). 모세가 돌아와 이 일로 그를 엄히 책망했으나, 아론은 그를 위해 중보하여 하나님께서 그 죄를 용서하셨다(신 9:20). 산에서 모세는 백성 가운데 세워질 예배 제도에 관한 지시를 받았고, 이에 따라 아론과 그 아들들은 제사장 직분으로 구별되었다(레 8; 9). 이후 아론은 대제사장으로서 그 직분에 합당한 중요한 지위를 차지하게 되었다. 이스라엘이 바란 광야의 하세롯에 이르렀을 때, 아론은 누이 미리암과 함께 모세가 구스 여인을 취한 것에 대해(아마도 십보라가 죽은 후) 그를 비방했다. 그러나 여호와께서 그의 종 모세를 변호하시고 미리암에게 나병을 내리셨다(민 12). 아론은 자신과 누이의 죄를 인정했고, 모세의 중보로 그들은 용서받았다. 그로부터 이십 년 후, 이스라엘 자손이 바란 광야에 진을 쳤을 때 고라, 다단, 아비람이 아론과 그 아들들을 대적하여 모반을 일으켰으나, 하나님의 무서운 심판이 그들에게 임하여 멸망했고, 이튿날 수많은 백성도 전염병으로 죽었는데 아론의 중재로써만 그 재앙이 멈췄다(민 16). 아론의 제사장 직분이 하나님께서 세우신 것임을 더욱 확증하기 위해 각 지파의 지도자들은 자기 지파의 이름을 새긴 지팡이를 모세에게 가져오게 했다. 이것들을 아론의 레위 지파 지팡이와 함께 장막 안에 하룻밤 두었더니, 아침에 보니 다른 지팡이들은 그대로였으나 아론의 지팡이만 싹이 나고 꽃이 피고 살구 열매를 맺었다(민 17:1-10). 이 지팡이는 이후 그의 제사장 임명에 대한 신적 증거의 기념물로 장막에 보관되었다(히 9:4). 아론은 므리바에서 형제 모세의 죄에 연루되어(민 20:8-13) 그로 인해 약속의 땅에 들어가지 못하게 되었다. 이스라엘 자손이 에돔 땅 변경에 있는 호르산에 이르렀을 때, 하나님의 명령에 따라 모세는 아론과 그 아들 엘르아살을 온 백성이 보는 앞에서 산꼭대기로 데리고 올라갔다. 거기서 그는 아론의 제사장 예복을 벗겨 엘르아살에게 입혔고, 아론은 산꼭대기에서 123세로 죽어 "자기 백성에게로 돌아갔다"(민 20:23-29; 신 10:6; 32:50). 온 이스라엘 족속이 그를 위해 삼십 일 동안 애곡했다. 아론의 두 아들은 그보다 먼저 살아남아 엘르아살의 가문은 엘리 시대까지 대제사장직을 이었고, 이다말의 가문은 엘리부터 솔로몬 시대까지 이어졌다. 아론의 다른 두 아들은 제단 향단에 "다른 불"을 드린 대담한 불경건함으로 인해 이미 죽임을 당했었다(레 10:1,2). 아랍인들은 지금도 호르산의 두 봉우리 중 하나에 있는 아론의 무덤 전승지를 경외심으로 보여주며, 그곳에는 이슬람 예배당이 세워져 있다. 그의 이름은 코란에도 언급되어 있으며, 랍비들의 저술 속에는 그에 관한 많은 전설적 이야기가 있다. 그는 처음으로 기름부음을 받은 제사장이었다. 그의 후손인 "아론의 집"은 전체적으로 제사장 직분을 구성했다. 다윗 시대에는 그 수가 매우 많았다(대상 12:27). 레위 지파의 다른 갈래들은 성전 봉사와 관련하여 부차적인 지위를 맡았다. 아론은 대제사장으로서의 공적 신분에 있어서 그리스도의 예표였다. 그의 제사장직은 "장차 올 좋은 것들의 그림자"였으며, 이스라엘 백성이 "다른 제사장" 곧 멜기세덱의 반차를 따른 자가 일어날 때를 바라보게 하려는 것이었다(히 6:20).

entries.definition: the descendants of Aaron, and therefore priests. Jehoiada, the father of Benaiah, led 3,700 Aaronites as "fighting men" to the support of David at Hebron (1 Chr. 12:27).
entries.definition_ko: 아론의 후손, 곧 제사장들. 브나야의 아버지 여호야다는 헤브론에서 다윗을 지지하는 "용사" 아론 자손 3,700명을 이끌었다(대상 12:27). 엘르아살(민 3:32)과 후대에는 사독(대상 27:17)이 그들의 우두머리였다.

entries.definition: destruction, the Hebrew name (equivalent to the Greek Apollyon, i.e., destroyer) of "the angel of the bottomless pit" (Rev. 9:11). It is rendered "destruction" in Job 28:22; 31:12; 26:6; Prov. 15:11; 27:20.
entries.definition_ko: "멸망," 무저갱의 사자(계 9:11)를 가리키는 히브리어 이름(헬라어 아볼루온, 곧 "파괴자"에 상응). 욥 28:22; 31:12; 26:6; 잠 15:11; 27:20에서는 "멸망"으로 번역되었다. 이 가운데 뒤의 세 곳에서는 개역판이 "아바돈"이라는 단어를 그대로 유지한다. 이 단어를 파괴 개념의 인격화로 볼 수도 있고, 죽은 자들의 영역인 스올로 볼 수도 있다.

entries.definition: one of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus's court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).
entries.definition_ko: 아하수에로 궁정의 일곱 내시 중 하나(에 1:10; 2:21).

entries.definition: stony (Heb. marg. "Amanah," perennial), the chief river of Damascus (2 Kings 5:12). Its modern name is Barada, the Chrysorrhoas, or "golden stream," of the Greeks.
entries.definition_ko: "돌이 많은"(마르그. "아마나," 늘 흐르는), 다메섹의 주요 강(왕하 5:12). 현대 이름은 바라다이며, 헬라인들은 크리소로아스("황금 시내")라 불렀다. 다메섹 북서쪽 약 23마일 지점의 안티레바논 산맥 골짜기에서 발원하여 잠시 남쪽으로 흐르다가 세 갈래로 나뉘는데, 가운데 갈래는 다메섹을 관통하고 나머지 둘은 도시 양쪽을 흘러 그렇지 않으면 메마를 땅에 아름다움과 비옥함을 더한다.

entries.definition: regions beyond; i.e., on the east of Jordan, a mountain, or rather a mountain-chain, over against Jericho, to the east and south-east of the Dead Sea, in the land of Moab.
entries.definition_ko: "저편의 지역들," 곧 요단 동편, 여리고 맞은편, 사해의 동남쪽에 있는 산 혹은 산맥. "비스가 산 정상"(곧 느보산, 그 봉우리 중 하나)에서 모세는 약속의 땅을 바라보았고(신 3:27; 32:49), 그곳에서 죽었다(34:1,5). 이스라엘 백성은 아르논을 건넌 후 아바림 산지에 진을 친 적이 있다(민 33:47,48).

entries.definition: This Syriac or Chaldee word is found three times in the New Testament (Mark 14:36; Rom. 8:15; Gal. 4:6), and in each case is followed by its Greek equivalent, which is translated "father."
entries.definition_ko: 이 시리아어 또는 갈대아어 단어는 신약에서 세 번 등장하며(막 14:36; 롬 8:15; 갈 4:6) 각 경우마다 그 헬라어 번역인 "아버지"가 뒤따른다. 따뜻한 애정과 자녀다운 확신을 표현하는 말로, 우리 언어에는 완전히 대응하는 말이 없다. 유럽 언어에는 교회 용어인 "아빠트(abbot)"로 전해졌다.

entries.definition: servant. (1.) The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., "levy"). (2.) A Levite of the family of Jeduthun (Neh. 11:17), also called Obadiah (1 Chr. 9:16).
entries.definition_ko: "종." (1.) 솔로몬이 조세(강제노역)를 관장하게 한 아도니람의 아버지(왕상 4:6). (2.) 여두둔 가문의 레위인(느 11:17), 오바댜라고도 불림(대상 9:16).

entries.definition: servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.
entries.definition_ko: "하나님의 종"(렘 36:26), 스마야의 아버지.

entries.definition: servant of God, (1 Chr. 5:15), a Gadite chief.
entries.definition_ko: "하나님의 종"(대상 5:15), 갓 지파의 지도자.

entries.definition: servile. (1.) The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Sam. 12:11.
entries.definition_ko: "종의." (1.) 힐렐의 아들, 비라돈 사람, 이스라엘의 열 번째 사사(삿 12:13-15). 삼상 12:11의 베단과 동일 인물로 추정된다. (2.) 기브온의 장자, 베냐민 지파(대상 8:30; 9:36). (3.) 미가의 아들, 요시야가 새로 발견된 율법책의 뜻을 물으라고 여선지 훌다에게 보낸 사람 중 하나(대하 34:20). 왕하 22:12에서는 악볼이라 불린다. (4.) 사삭의 "아들들" 중 하나(대상 8:23). 아셀 지파에 속한 게르손 자손의 레위 성읍의 이름이기도 하다(수 21:30; 대상 6:74). 악고 북동쪽 약 8마일 지점의 압데 유적이 그 위치로 추정된다.

entries.definition: servant of Nego=Nebo, the Chaldee name given to Azariah, one of Daniel's three companions (Dan. 2:49). With Shadrach and Meshach, he was delivered from the burning fiery furnace (3:12-30).
entries.definition_ko: "느고(느보)의 종," 다니엘의 세 동료 중 하나인 아사랴에게 붙여진 갈대아 이름(단 2:49). 사드락, 메삭과 함께 맹렬히 타는 풀무불에서 구원받았다(3:12-30).

entries.definition: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain (Gen. 4:1-16).
entries.definition_ko: (히브리어 헤벨), "숨" 또는 "헛됨," 아담과 하와의 둘째 아들. 형 가인에게 죽임을 당했다(창 4:1-16). 아버지의 가르침을 따라 두 형제는 하나님을 예배하도록 훈련받았다. "때가 되어"(마르그. "날들이 끝날 때," 곧 안식일) 각자 자기 수고의 첫 열매를 하나님께 드렸다. 농부였던 가인은 땅의 소산을, 목자였던 아벨은 양 떼의 첫 새끼를 드렸다. "여호와께서 아벨과 그의 제물은 열납하셨으나 가인과 그의 제물은 열납하지 아니하셨다"(창 4:3-5). 이로 인해 가인은 아우에게 분노하여 그를 죽일 계획을 세웠고, 마침내 그 뜻을 이루었다(창 4:8,9; 비교. 요일 3:12). 신약에는 아벨에 관한 언급이 여러 번 나온다. 우리 구주께서는 그를 "의로운" 자로 부르셨다(마 23:35). "뿌린 피"는 "아벨의 피보다 더 나은 것을 말한다"(히 12:24)고 하는데, 이는 그리스도의 피가 아벨이 드린 제물의 피가 예표했던 실체임을 뜻한다. 여기서 비교는 그리스도께서 드리신 제사와 아벨이 드린 제사 사이의 것이지, 자비를 구하는 그리스도의 피와 복수를 부르짖는 아벨의 피 사이의 것이 아니다(간혹 그렇게 오해되기도 함). 또한 "아벨은 믿음으로 가인보다 더 나은 제사를 하나님께 드렸다"(히 11:4)고 한다. 이 제사는 "믿음으로" 드려진 것으로, 이 믿음은 창조주요 섭리의 하나님으로서만이 아니라 특별히 구속자이신 하나님을 향한 것이었으며, 그의 희생제사는 아담 이후로 신적 제정에 의해 드려져 온 제사들이 예표한 것이었다. 장차 올 위대한 속죄 제사를 바라본 그 "믿음" 때문에 아벨의 제물은 하나님께 받아들여졌다. 가인의 제물에는 그런 관련이 없었기에 배척되었다. 아벨은 최초의 순교자였으며, 우리 인류 중 최초로 죽은 자였다.

entries.definition: meadow of the house of Maachah, a city in the north of Palestine, in the neighbourhood of Dan and Ijon, in the tribe of Naphtali.
entries.definition_ko: "마아가 집의 초장," 팔레스타인 북부, 단과 이욘 근처, 납달리 지파에 있는 성읍. 상당한 견고함과 중요성을 지닌 곳이었다. "이스라엘의 어미"라 불렸는데(삼하 20:19), 이는 곧 수도라는 뜻이다. 요압(삼하 20:14), 벤하닷(왕상 15:20), 디글랏빌레셀(왕하 15:29, 주전 734년경)에게 포위 공격을 받았다. 다른 곳에서는 "물들의 초장"이라는 뜻의 아벨마임이라 불린다(대하 16:4).

entries.definition: (Judg. 11:33, R.V.; A. V., "plain of the vineyards"), a village of the Ammonites, whither Jephthah pursued their forces.
entries.definition_ko: (삿 11:33, R.V.; A.V.에는 "포도원의 평지"), 암몬 사람들의 마을로 입다가 그들의 군대를 그곳까지 추격했다.

entries.definition: meadow of dancing, or the dancing-meadow, the birth-place and residence of the prophet Elisha, not far from Beth-shean (1 Kings 4:12), in the tribe of Issachar.
entries.definition_ko: "춤의 초장," 선지자 엘리사의 출생지이자 거주지, 벧산에서 멀지 않은 곳(왕상 4:12), 잇사갈 지파에 속함.

entries.definition: meadow of Egypt, or mourning of Egypt, a place "beyond," i.e., on the west of Jordan, at the "threshing-floor of Atad."
entries.definition_ko: "애굽의 초장" 또는 "애굽의 애곡," 요단 "저편," 곧 서편에 있는 곳, "아닷의 타작마당."

entries.definition: meadow of the acacias, frequently called simply "Shittim" (Num. 25:1; Josh. 2:1; Micah 6:5), a place on the east of Jordan, in the plain of Moab.
entries.definition_ko: "아카시아의 초장," 흔히 "싯딤"이라고만 불림(민 25:1; 수 2:1; 미 6:5), 요단 동편 모압 평지에 있는 곳.

entries.definition: tin, or white, a town in the tribe of Issachar (Josh. 19:20), at the north of the plain of Esdraelon.
entries.definition_ko: "주석" 또는 "흰," 잇사갈 지파의 성읍(수 19:20), 에스드라엘론 평야 북쪽.

entries.definition: my father is the Lord, the Greek form of Abijah, or Abijam (Matt. 1:7), instead of Abiah (1 Chr. 7:8).
entries.definition_ko: "나의 아버지는 여호와시다," 아비야 또는 아비얌의 헬라어 형태(마 1:7), 대상 7:8의 아비아 대신 쓰임.

entries.definition: father of strength; i.e., "valiant", one of David's body-guard of thirty mighty men (2 Sam. 23:31); called also Abiel (1 Chr. 11:32).
entries.definition_ko: "힘의 아버지," 곧 "용맹한," 다윗의 삼십 용사 중 하나(삼하 23:31); 대상 11:32에서는 아비엘이라고도 불림.

entries.definition: father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).
entries.definition_ko: "모음의 아버지," 곧 모으는 자, 레위인 고라의 세 아들 중 막내, 고핫 가문의 수장(출 6:24); 대상 6:37에서는 에비아삽이라 불림.

entries.definition: father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.
entries.definition_ko: "풍성함의 아버지," 곧 "나의 아버지가 뛰어나시다," 대제사장 아히멜렉의 아들. 그는 열 번째 대제사장이었고 엘리로부터 4대손이었다.

entries.definition: an ear of corn, the month of newly-ripened grain (Ex. 13:4; 23:15); the first of the Jewish ecclesiastical year, and the seventh of the civil year.
entries.definition_ko: "곡식의 이삭," 새로 익은 곡식의 달(출 13:4; 23:15); 유대 종교력의 첫째 달이자 민간력의 일곱째 달.

entries.definition: or Abi'dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33).
entries.definition_ko: "아비다" 또는 "지식의 아버지," 미디안의 다섯 아들 중 하나, 아브라함이 그두라에게서 낳은 아들(대상 1:33).

entries.definition: father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).
entries.definition_ko: "심판의 아버지," 곧 재판장, 출애굽 당시 베냐민 지파의 수장(민 1:11; 2:22).

entries.definition: father of help; i.e., "helpful." (1.) The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead.
entries.definition_ko: "도움의 아버지," 곧 "돕는 자." (1.) 길르앗의 누이 함몰레겟의 세 아들 중 둘째.

entries.definition: father (i.e., "possessor") of God = "pious." (1.) The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39).
entries.definition_ko: "하나님의(곧 소유자의) 아버지," 곧 "경건한." (1.) 스롤의 아들이자 넬의 아버지, 사울의 조부(삼상 14:51; 대상 8:33; 9:39).

entries.definition: father of help, a descendant of Abiezer (Judg. 6:11,24; 8:32).
entries.definition_ko: "도움의 아버지," 아비에셀의 후손(삿 6:11,24; 8:32).

entries.definition: father (i.e., "leader") of the dance, or "of joy." (1.) The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite (1 Chr. 2:16,17).
entries.definition_ko: "춤의(곧 인도자의) 아버지," 곧 "기쁨의." (1.) 다윗의 누이, 이스마엘 사람 예델의 아내(대상 2:16,17).

entries.definition: father of might. (1.) Num. 3:35. (2.) 1 Chr. 2:29. (3.) 1 Chr. 5:14. (4.) The second wife of King Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:18).
father of Him; i.e., "worshipper of God", the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3).
entries.definition_ko: "그의 아버지," 곧 "하나님의 예배자," 아론의 둘째 아들(출 6:23; 민 3:2; 26:60; 대상 6:3).

entries.definition: father (i.e., "possessor") of renown. (1.) One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:3); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).
entries.definition_ko: "명성의(곧 소유자의) 아버지." (1.) 베냐민의 아들 벨라의 아들 중 하나(대상 8:3); 아히훗이라고도 불림(7절).

entries.definition: father (i.e., "possessor or worshipper") of Jehovah. (1.) 1 Chr. 7:8. (2.) 1 Chr. 2:24.
entries.definition_ko: "여호와의(곧 소유자 또는 예배자의) 아버지." (1.) 대상 7:8. (2.) 대상 2:24.

entries.definition: father of the sea; i.e., "seaman" the name always used in Kings of the king of Judah, the son of Rehoboam, elsewhere called Abijah (1 Kings 15:1,7,8).
entries.definition_ko: "바다의 아버지," 곧 "뱃사람," 열왕기에서 항상 사용되는 유다 왕 르호보암의 아들의 이름, 다른 곳에서는 아비야라 불림(왕상 15:1,7,8).

entries.definition: a plain, a district lying on the east slope of the Anti-Lebanon range; so called from its chief town, Abila (Luke 3:1).
entries.definition_ko: 평야, 안티레바논 산맥 동쪽 비탈에 있는 지역; 주된 성읍인 아빌라에서 그 이름이 유래함(눅 3:1).

entries.definition: father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).
entries.definition_ko: "마엘의 아버지," 요단 북부 아라비아에 살던 욕단의 아들 또는 후손 중 하나(창 10:28; 대상 1:22).

entries.definition: my father a king, or father of a king, a common name of the Philistine kings, as "Pharaoh" was of the Egyptian kings.
entries.definition_ko: "왕이신 나의 아버지," 곧 "왕의 아버지," 애굽 왕들이 "바로"라 불렸던 것처럼 블레셋 왕들의 공통 칭호.

entries.definition: father of nobleness; i.e., "noble." (1.) A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1).
entries.definition_ko: "고귀함의 아버지," 곧 "고귀한." (1.) 기럇여아림의 레위인으로, 그의 집에 언약궤가 블레셋 땅에서 돌아온 후 보관되었다(삼상 7:1).

entries.definition: father of kindness, the father of Barak (Judg. 4:6; 5:1).
entries.definition_ko: "인자함의 아버지," 바락의 아버지(삿 4:6; 5:1).

entries.definition: father of height; i.e., "proud." (1.) One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron.
entries.definition_ko: "높음의 아버지," 곧 "교만한." (1.) 엘리압의 아들 중 하나로 고라와 함께 모세와 아론을 대적하는 모반에 가담했다.

entries.definition: father of (i.e., "given to") error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age.
entries.definition_ko: "(곧 '주어진')의 아버지 오류," 미모로 이름난 수넴 여인. 다윗의 노년에 그를 시중들도록 선택되었다.

entries.definition: father of (i.e., "desirous of") a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David's sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16).
entries.definition_ko: "(곧 '갈망하는')의 아버지," 선물, 다윗의 누이 스루야의 맏아들. 요압과 아사헬의 형제(삼하 2:18; 대상 2:16).

entries.definition: father of welfare; i.e., "fortunate." (1.) The grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4). (2.) The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4,5,50; Ezra 7:5).
entries.definition_ko: "복지의 아버지," 곧 "복 있는." (1.) 베냐민의 손자(대상 8:4). (2.) 대제사장 비느하스의 아들(대상 6:4,5,50; 스 7:5).

entries.definition: father of the wall; i.e., "mason", one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28,29).
entries.definition_ko: "벽의 아버지," 곧 "석공," 유다 지파 삼매의 두 아들 중 하나(대상 2:28,29).

entries.definition: father of dew; i.e., "fresh", David's fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).
entries.definition_ko: "이슬의 아버지," 곧 "신선한," 다윗의 다섯째 아내(삼하 3:4).

entries.definition: father of goodness, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:11).
entries.definition_ko: "선함의 아버지," 베냐민 사람(대상 8:11).

entries.definition: (Ps. 35:15), the translation of a Hebrew word meaning smiters; probably, in allusion to the tongue, slanderers. (Comp. Jer. 18:18.)
entries.definition_ko: (시 35:15), "때리는 자"를 뜻하는 히브리어 단어의 번역; 아마도 혀에 빗대어, 비방자를 가리킴(비교. 렘 18:18).

entries.definition: or washing, was practised, (1.) When a person was initiated into a higher state: e.g., when Aaron and his sons were set apart to the priest's office, they were washed with water previous to their investiture with the priestly robes (Lev. 8:6).
entries.definition_ko: 또는 씻음, (1.) 사람이 더 높은 신분으로 들어갈 때 행해졌다. 예를 들어 아론과 그 아들들이 제사장 직분으로 구별될 때, 그들은 제사장 예복을 입기 전에 물로 씻겨졌다(레 8:6). (2.) 제사장들이 하나님의 제단에 나아가기 전, 죽음을 면하기 위해 손과 발을 씻어 일상의 더러움을 씻어내야 했다(출 30:17-21). 시편 기자는 이 관행을 언급한다(시 26:6). (3.) 특정 행위로 인한 실제적인 부정을 씻기 위한 씻음도 있었다. 이런 씻음은 레위기 율법에 열한 가지 종류로 규정되어 있다(레 12-15). (4.) 네 번째 부류는 어떤 특정 행위의 죄책으로부터 스스로를 정결케 하거나 사면받는 씻음이다. 예를 들어 살인자를 알 수 없을 때, 살인이 일어난 곳에서 가장 가까운 마을의 장로들은 목이 꺾인 암송아지 위에서 손을 씻으며 "우리 손이 이 피를 흘리지 아니하였고 우리 눈도 보지 못하였나이다"라고 말해야 했다(신 21:1-9). 빌라도도 손을 씻음으로써 예수의 피에 대해 자신은 무죄하다고 선언했다(마 27:24). 빌라도의 이 행위는 유대인의 관습에서 빌려온 것이 아닐 수도 있다. 이와 같은 관행은 헬라인과 로마인 사이에서도 흔했다. 바리새인들은 씻음의 관행을 지나치게 행하여 특별한 정결함을 주장했다(마 23:25). 마가복음(7:1-5)은 이 의식적 씻음을 언급한다. 바리새인들은 손을 "부지런히"(더 정확히는 "주먹까지," 개역판 "정성스럽게") 씻었는데, 고대 교부 테오필락투스는 이를 "팔꿈치까지"라고 설명한다(비교. 막 7:4; 레 6:28; 11:32-36; 15:22).

entries.definition: father of light; i.e., "enlightening", the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul's army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).
entries.definition_ko: "빛의 아버지," 곧 "빛을 비추는," 넬의 아들이자 사울의 삼촌. 사울 군대의 총사령관이었다(삼상 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

entries.definition: This word is used, (1.) To express the idea that the Egyptians considered themselves as defiled when they ate with strangers (Gen. 43:32).
entries.definition_ko: 이 단어는 다음과 같이 사용된다. (1.) 애굽인들이 이방인과 함께 식사하는 것을 부정하게 여긴다는 개념을 표현하기 위해(창 43:32).

entries.definition: father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises.
entries.definition_ko: "많은 무리의 아버지," 데라의 아들, 형들인 나홀과 하란보다 먼저 언급되는데(창 11:27) 이는 그가 약속의 상속자였기 때문이다.

entries.definition: (Luke 16:22,23) refers to the custom of reclining on couches at table, which was prevalent among the Jews, an arrangement which brought the head of one person almost into the bosom of the one who sat or reclined above him.
entries.definition_ko: (눅 16:22,23), 유대인들 사이에 널리 퍼져 있던 식탁에서 비스듬히 기대어 눕는 관습을 가리키는데, 이 배치는 한 사람의 머리가 자기 위쪽에 앉거나 기댄 사람의 품 가까이 오게 하는 것이었다.

entries.definition: exalted father.
entries.definition_ko: "높임받은 아버지."

entries.definition: R.V., one of Israel's halting-places in the desert (Num.33:34,35), just before Ezion-gaber. In A.V., "Ebronah."
entries.definition_ko: R.V., 광야에서 이스라엘의 머무는 곳 중 하나(민 33:34,35), 에시온게벨 바로 앞. A.V.에서는 "에브로나."

entries.definition: father of peace; i.e., "peaceful" David's son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).
entries.definition_ko: "평화의 아버지," 곧 "평화로운," 다윗이 마아가에게서 낳은 아들(삼하 3:3; 비교. 왕상 1:6). 그는 준수한 외모와 머리털의 유별난 숱 많음으로 유명했다(삼하 14:25,26). 그의 생애 첫 공적 행위는 다윗의 맏아들 암논에 대한 피의 보복이었는데, 암논이 압살롬의 누이 다말을 비열하게 욕보였기 때문이다. 이 복수는 바알하솔에서 열린 큰 양털 깎는 잔치 때 행해졌다. 다윗의 다른 아들들은 그곳에서 두려움에 도망하여 암논의 죽음을 예루살렘에 알렸다. 자신의 행위 결과를 두려워한 압살롬은 그술에 있는 외조부에게 도망하여 삼 년간 머물렀다(삼하 3:3; 13:23-38). 다윗은 이제 형제살해의 죄를 지닌 채 떠나 있는 아들을 위해 애통해했다. 드고아 여인이 꾸민 계략의 결과로, 요압은 압살롬을 예루살렘으로 다시 부르라는 다윗의 허락을 얻었다. 그는 이렇게 돌아왔으나, 이 년이 지나서야 아버지 앞에 나아갈 수 있었다(삼하 14:28). 압살롬은 이제 다윗의 생존한 아들 중 가장 나이가 많았고, 어머니와 아버지 양쪽으로 왕족 혈통이었기에 왕위를 탐내기 시작했다. 그의 야망은 백성의 지지를 받았다. 여러 술책으로 그들의 마음을 얻었고, 그술에서 돌아온 후(삼하 15:7) 유다의 옛 수도 헤브론으로 올라가 많은 백성을 이끌고 그곳에서 자신을 왕으로 선포했다. 반란이 매우 성공적이어서 다윗은 예루살렘을 떠나 요단 건너 마하나임으로 피할 수밖에 없었고, 압살롬은 예루살렘으로 돌아와 아무 저항 없이 왕좌를 차지했다. 다윗의 수석 모사였던 아히도벨은 그를 배반하고 압살롬에게 가담하여 이제 그의 수석 모사가 되었다. 후새도 압살롬에게 가담했지만, 이는 오직 아히도벨의 계략을 방해하여 다윗의 대의에 유익을 주려는 목적이었다. 그는 어느 정도 성공하여, 아히도벨의 조언 대신 그의 조언이 받아들여져 압살롬은 아버지를 향해 진군하는 것을 늦추었고, 다윗은 방어를 준비할 시간을 얻었다. 마침내 압살롬은 아버지를 대적하여 진군했고, 요압이 지휘하는 다윗의 군대와 에브라임 숲 경계에서 마주쳤다. 그 치명적인 전투에서 압살롬의 군대 이만 명이 죽었고 나머지는 도망쳤다. 압살롬은 빠른 노새를 타고 도망쳤으나, 길게 늘어뜨린 머리(혹은 더 정확히는 머리 자체)가 상수리나무 가지에 걸려 매달리게 되었고, 그곳에서 요압이 이르러 창 셋으로 그를 찔러 죽였다. 그의 시신은 내려져 숲 속에 판 구덩이에 던져졌고, 그 위에 돌무더기를 쌓았다. 그 전투의 결과가 마하나임 성문에서 초조하게 기다리던 다윗에게 전해지고 압살롬이 죽었다는 말을 들었을 때, 그는 애통하며 부르짖었다. "내 아들 압살롬아, 내 아들, 내 아들 압살롬아! 차라리 내가 너를 대신하여 죽었더라면, 압살롬 내 아들아, 내 아들아!"(삼하 18:33; 비교. 출 32:32; 롬 9:3). 압살롬의 세 아들(삼하 14:27; 비교. 18:18)은 모두 그보다 먼저 죽었으므로, 그는 딸 다말만을 남겼는데, 그녀는 후에 아비야의 조모가 되었다.

entries.definition: (Heb. shittim) Ex. 25:5, R.V. probably the Acacia seyal (the gum-arabic tree); called the "shittah" tree (Isa. 41:19).
entries.definition_ko: (히브리어 싯딤) 출 25:5, R.V.는 아카시아 세얄(고무아라비아 나무)로 본다; "싯딤" 나무라 불림(사 41:19). 그 목재는 싯딤 나무라 불린다(출 26:15,26; 25:10,13,23,28 등). 이 종(A. seyal)은 산사나무와 비슷하며 옹이가 많고 가시가 있다. 시내 반도에 풍부하게 자생한다.

entries.definition: the high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon.
entries.definition_ko: "높은 땅 또는 산지," 시날 땅의 성읍. 바벨론 북쪽 약 50마일 지점의 악커 쿠프 유적과 동일시되기도 한다(확실치는 않음). 니므롯 왕국의 성읍 중 하나였다(창 10:10).

entries.definition: sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them (Judg. 1:31).
entries.definition_ko: "무더운 또는 모래의," 아셀 지파에 속했으나 결코 그들에게 정복되지 않은 페니키아의 항구 도시(삿 1:31).

entries.definition: Satan is styled the "accuser of the brethren" (Rev. 12:10. Comp. Job 1:6; Zech. 3:1), as seeking to uphold his influence among men by bringing false charges against Christians.
entries.definition_ko: 사탄은 "형제들을 참소하는 자"라 불린다(계 12:10; 비교. 욥 1:6; 슥 3:1). 이는 그리스도인들에게 거짓 고발을 함으로써 사람들 가운데 자신의 영향력을 유지하려 하기 때문이다.

entries.definition: the name which the Jews gave in their proper tongue, i.e., in Aramaic, to the field which was purchased with the money which had been given to the betrayer of our Lord. The word means "field of blood."
entries.definition_ko: 우리 주를 배반한 자에게 주었던 돈으로 산 밭에 유대인들이 자기 나라 말, 곧 아람어로 붙인 이름. 이 말은 "피밭"을 뜻한다.

entries.definition: the name originally of a narrow strip of territory in Greece, on the north-west of the Peloponnesus.
entries.definition_ko: 본래 그리스에서 펠로폰네소스 반도 북서쪽의 좁은 지역의 이름.

entries.definition: (1 Cor. 16:17), one of the members of the church of Corinth who, with Fortunatus and Stephanas, visited Paul while he was at Ephesus.
entries.definition_ko: (고전 16:17), 고린도 교회의 일원으로 브드나도와 스데바나와 함께 에베소에 있던 바울을 방문한 사람.

entries.definition: called also Achar, i.e., one who troubles (1 Chr. 2:7), in commemoration of his crime, which brought upon him an awful destruction (Josh. 7:1).
entries.definition_ko: 아갈이라고도 불리며, 곧 "말썽꾼"(대상 2:7), 그의 범죄를 기념하는 이름인데, 이 죄로 인해 그는 끔찍한 파멸을 당했다(수 7:1).

entries.definition: gnawing, = mouse. (1.) An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).
angry, perhaps only a general title of royalty applicable to the Philistine kings.
entries.definition_ko: "성난," 아마도 블레셋 왕들에게 적용되던 일반적인 왕실 칭호였을 것이다.

entries.definition: (Ezra 6:2), called Ecbatana by classical writers, the capital of northern Media.
entries.definition_ko: (스 6:2), 고전 저술가들에 의해 엑바타나라 불렸으며, 북부 메대의 수도였다.

entries.definition: trouble, a valley near Jericho, so called in consequence of the trouble which the sin of Achan caused Israel (Josh. 7:24,26).
entries.definition_ko: "괴로움," 여리고 근처의 골짜기, 아간의 죄로 이스라엘이 겪은 고난 때문에 이렇게 불렸다(수 7:24,26).

entries.definition: anklet, Caleb's only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.
entries.definition_ko: "발목장식," 갈렙의 외동딸(대상 2:49). 그녀는 드빌 곧 기럇세벨 성읍을 공격하여 이끄는 사람에게 혼인으로 주어졌다.

entries.definition: fascination, a royal city of the Canaanites, in the north of Palestine (Josh. 11:1; 12:20; 19:25).
entries.definition_ko: "매혹," 팔레스타인 북부에 있는 가나안 사람들의 왕도(수 11:1; 12:20; 19:25).

entries.definition: falsehood. (1.) A town in the Shephelah, or plain country of Judah (Josh. 15:44).
entries.definition_ko: "거짓됨." (1.) 유다의 평지, 곧 세펠라에 있는 성읍(수 15:44).

entries.definition: is the translation of a word (tse'med), which properly means a yoke, and denotes a space of ground that may be ploughed by a yoke of oxen in a day.
entries.definition_ko: "멍에"를 뜻하는 단어(체메드)의 번역으로, 소 한 겨리가 하루에 갈 수 있는 넓이의 땅을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: the title now given to the fifth and last of the historical books of the New Testament. The author styles it a "treatise" (1:1).
entries.definition_ko: 신약의 역사서 중 다섯 번째이자 마지막 책에 지금 붙여진 제목. 저자는 이를 "논술"이라 부른다(1:1).

entries.definition: ornament. (1.) The first of Lamech's two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).
entries.definition_ko: "장식." (1.) 라멕의 두 아내 중 첫째, 야발과 유발의 어머니(창 4:19,20,23).

entries.definition: red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages.
entries.definition_ko: "붉은," 바벨론어 단어로 사람을 가리키는 일반명사이며 히브리어와 앗수르어에서 같은 뜻을 지닌다.

entries.definition: red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias (Josh. 19:33, 36).
entries.definition_ko: "붉은 흙," 납달리의 요새화된 성읍, 아마도 현대의 다미에, 디베랴 바다 서편(수 19:33,36).

entries.definition: (Heb. shamir), Ezek. 3:9. The Greek word adamas means diamond. This stone is not referred to, but corundum or some kind of hard steel.
entries.definition_ko: (히브리어 샤미르), 겔 3:9. 헬라어 아다마스는 다이아몬드를 뜻한다. 이 돌 자체를 가리키는 것은 아니고, 강옥 혹은 일종의 단단한 강철을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: The apostle Paul speaks of Adam as "the figure of him who was to come." On this account our Lord is sometimes called the second Adam.
entries.definition_ko: 사도 바울은 아담을 "장차 오실 이의 모형"으로 말한다. 이 때문에 우리 주님은 때때로 둘째 아담이라 불린다.

entries.definition: is referred to in Josh. 3:16. It stood "beside Zarethan," on the west bank of Jordan (1 Kings 4:12).
entries.definition_ko: 수 3:16에 언급됨. "사르단 곁," 요단 서쪽 강둑에 있었다(왕상 4:12).

entries.definition: large, the sixth month of the civil and the twelfth of the ecclesiastical year of the Jews (Esther 3:7, 13; 8:12; 9:1, 15, 17, 19, 21).
entries.definition_ko: "큰," 유대인 민간력의 여섯째 달이자 종교력의 열두째 달(에 3:7,13; 8:12; 9:1,15,17,19,21).

entries.definition: miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).
entries.definition_ko: "하나님의 기적," 이스마엘의 열두 아들 중 셋째, 아라비아 한 지파의 우두머리(창 25:13; 대상 1:29).

entries.definition: ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chr. 8:3); called also "Ard" (Gen. 46:21)
entries.definition_ko: "넓은, 화려한," 벨라의 아들(대상 8:3); "아릇"이라고도 불림(창 46:21).

entries.definition: (Ps. 140:3; Rom. 3:13, "asp") is the rendering of, (1.) Akshub ("coiling" or "lying in wait"), properly an asp or viper, found only in this passage.
entries.definition_ko: (시 140:3; 롬 3:13, "독사"), 다음의 번역이다. (1.) 악슈브("사리다" 또는 "매복하다"), 본래 살무사나 독사, 이 구절에서만 발견됨.

entries.definition: ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.
entries.definition_ko: "장식," (눅 3:28), 고삼의 아들이자 멜기의 아버지, 그리스도의 조상 중 한 사람.

entries.definition: low, one of the persons named in Neh. 7:61 who could not "shew their father's house" on the return from captivity.
entries.definition_ko: "낮은," 느헤미야 7:61에 언급된 사람 중 하나로, 포로에서 돌아왔을 때 "자기 조상의 집"을 증명하지 못한 자.

entries.definition: ornament of God. (1.) The father of Azmaveth, who was treasurer under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:25).
entries.definition_ko: "하나님의 장식." (1.) 다윗과 솔로몬 시대에 재무관이었던 아스마웻의 아버지(대상 27:25).

entries.definition: effeminate. (1.) Ezra 8:6. (2.) Neh. 10:16.
slender, one of David's warriors (1 Chr. 11:42), a Reubenite.
entries.definition_ko: "가느다란," 다윗의 용사 중 하나(대상 11:42), 르우벤 사람.

entries.definition: the Eznite, one of David's mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).
entries.definition_ko: "에스나 사람," 다윗의 용사 중 하나(삼하 23:8).

entries.definition: a solemn appeal whereby one person imposes on another the obligation of speaking or acting as if under an oath (1 Sam. 14:24; Josh. 6:26; 1 Kings 22:16).
entries.definition_ko: 한 사람이 다른 사람에게 마치 맹세 아래 있는 것처럼 말하거나 행동할 의무를 지우는 엄숙한 요청(삼상 14:24; 수 6:26; 왕상 22:16).

entries.definition: earth, one of the five cities of the vale of Siddim (Gen. 10:19). It was destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah (19:24; Deut. 29:23).
entries.definition_ko: "흙," 시딤 골짜기의 다섯 성읍 중 하나(창 10:19). 소돔, 고모라와 함께 멸망했다(19:24; 신 29:23).

entries.definition: delight. (1.) A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20). (2.) A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men (2 Chr. 17:14).
entries.definition_ko: "기쁨." (1.) 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 므낫세 지파의 지도자(대상 12:20). (2.) 여호사밧 아래 30만 명을 거느린 장군(대하 17:14).

entries.definition: lord of Bezek, a Canaanitish king who, having subdued seventy of the chiefs that were around him, made an attack against the armies of Judah and Simeon.
entries.definition_ko: "베섹의 주," 자기 주위의 일흔 왕을 굴복시킨 후 유다와 시므온의 군대를 공격한 가나안 왕.

entries.definition: my Lord is Jehovah. (1.) The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne.
entries.definition_ko: "나의 주는 여호와시다." (1.) 다윗의 넷째 아들(삼하 3:4). 형들인 암논과 압살롬이 죽은 후 그는 왕위 계승자로 여겨지게 되었다.

entries.definition: whom the Lord sets up, one of those "which came with Zerubbabel" (Ezra 2:13).
entries.definition_ko: "주께서 세우신 자," 스룹바벨과 함께 온 자 중 하나(스 2:13).

entries.definition: (Adoram, 1 Kings 12:18), the son of Abda, was "over the tribute," i.e., the levy or forced labour.
entries.definition_ko: (아도람, 왕상 12:18), 압다의 아들, 조세, 곧 강제노역을 관장하는 자였다.

entries.definition: lord of justice or righteousness, was king in Jerusalem at the time when the Israelites invaded Palestine (Josh. 10:1,3).
entries.definition_ko: "의의 주" 또는 "정의의 주," 이스라엘이 팔레스타인을 침공했을 때 예루살렘에서 왕이었다(수 10:1,3).

entries.definition: lord. (1.) The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17). Baal is identified with Molech (Jer. 19:5). It was known to the Israelites as Baal-peor, was worshipped till the time of Samuel, and was afterwards the religion of the ten tribes in the time of Ahab. (2.) A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36). (3.) The name of a place inhabited by the Simeonites, the same probably as Baal-ath-beer (1 Chr. 4:33; Josh. 19:8).
mistress; city. A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29), elsewhere called Balah (Josh. 19:3) and Bilhah (1 Chr. 4:29). Now Khurbet Zebalah.
a town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:44). It was fortified by Solomon (1 Kings 9:18; 2 Chr. 8:6).
Baalah of the well (Josh. 19:8), probably the same as Baal, mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:33, a city of Simeon.

called by the Greeks Heliopolis, i.e., "the city of the sun," because of its famous Temple of the Sun. It was a city of Coele-Syria, on the lowest declivity of Anti-Libanus, about 42 miles north-west of Damascus, finally destroyed by an earthquake in 1759.
covenant lord, the name of the god worshipped in Shechem after the death of Gideon (Judg. 8:33; 9:4).
lords of Judah, a city in the tribe of Judah from which David brought the ark into Jerusalem (2 Sam. 6:2). Elsewhere called Kirjath-jearim.
lord of fortune, or troop of Baal, a Canaanite city in the valley of Lebanon at the foot of Hermon, near the source of the Jordan.
place of a multitude, a place where Solomon had an extensive vineyard (Cant. 8:11).
lord of grace. (1.) A king of Edom, son of Achbor. (2.) An overseer of "the olive trees and sycomore trees" under David.
having a courtyard, or Baal's village, the place where Absalom held the feast of sheep-shearing when Amnon was assassinated (2 Sam. 13:23).
lord of Hermon, a city near Mount Hermon inhabited by the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 5:23).
my lord, a title the prophet (Hos. 2:16) reproaches the Jewish church for applying to Jehovah, instead of the more endearing title Ishi, meaning "my husband."
plural of Baal; images of the god Baal (Judg. 2:11; 1 Sam. 7:4).
king of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah.
lord of dwelling, a town of Reuben (Num. 32:38), called also Beth-meon.
lord of the opening, a god of the Moabites (Num. 25:3; 31:16; Josh. 22:17), worshipped by obscene rites.
Baal having rents, bursts, or destructions, the scene of a victory gained by David over the Philistines (2 Sam. 5:20; 1 Chr. 14:11).
lord of Shalisha, a place from which a man brought provisions to Elisha, apparently not far from Gilgal (2 Kings 4:42).
lord of palm trees, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Gibeah of Saul (Judg. 20:33), one of the sanctuaries of Baal.
fly-lord, the god of the Philistines at Ekron (2 Kings 1:2, 3, 16), supposed able to avert the plague of flies. He was consulted by Ahaziah as to his recovery.
Baal of the north, an Egyptian town on the shores of the Gulf of Suez (Ex. 14:2; Num. 33:7), over against which Israel encamped before crossing the Red Sea.
son of affliction. (1.) One of Solomon's purveyors (1 Kings 4:12). (2.) Son of Hushai, another purveyor. (3.) Father of Zadok (Neh. 3:4).
son of affliction. One of two sons of Rimmon the Beerothite who assassinated Ishbosheth (2 Sam. 4:2), and were slain by David for it.

bravery, third king of the separate kingdom of Israel and founder of its second dynasty (1 Kings 15-16), son of Ahijah of Issachar, reigned twenty-four years from Tirzah; his family was later exterminated for his idolatry.
used of children generally (Matt. 11:25), and also of those weak in Christian faith and knowledge (1 Cor. 3:1; Heb. 5:13).
the tower built in the land of Shinar after the Deluge (Gen. 11:1-9), meant as a rallying point to prevent the people being scattered; God confounded their language, hence "confusion."
the Greek form of Babel, capital of the Babylonian empire on the Euphrates, made splendid under Nebuchadnezzar, captured by Cyrus in B.C. 538, and eventually reduced to ruins.
a robe of rich colours fabricated at Babylon, hence of great value (Josh. 7:21).
"the land of the Chaldeans," an extensive province along the Tigris valley, famed for fertility and riches, whose capital was Babylon.
(Ps. 84:6), probably a valley in Palestine through which pilgrims passed on their way to the sanctuary, or figuratively "a valley of weeping."
to run about tattling or calumniating (Ps. 15:3); secret talebearing (Prov. 25:23); maliciously defaming the absent (Rom. 1:30).
to draw back or apostatize in matters of religion (Acts 21:21; 2 Thess. 2:3), which may be partial or complete.
the tabernacle covering rendered "badgers' skins" (Ex. 25:5) is now understood as sealskins or dugong hide, per the Revised Version.
several Hebrew words denote pouches for weights, money, or provisions carried by travellers (Deut. 25:13; Prov. 7:20); Judas kept "the bag" (John 12:6).
young men, a place east of Jerusalem (2 Sam. 3:16; 19:16) where Shimei cursed David and Jonathan and Ahimaaz hid.
house, probably a city of Moab with a celebrated idol-temple (Isa. 15:2).
bread-making was usually done by women or slaves; public bakers appear later (Hos. 7:4); ovens or hot pebbles were used (1 Kings 19:6).
baked provisions (Gen. 40:17), literally "works of the baker."
son of Beor, a Midianite diviner hired by Balak to curse Israel, but constrained by God to bless them instead (Num. 22-24); later slain fighting for Balak (Num. 31:8).
he has given a son, father of the Babylonian king Merodach-baladan (2 Kings 20:12).
a city in the tribe of Simeon (Josh. 19:3), elsewhere called Bilhah and Baalah.
empty; spoiler, son of Zippor and king of the Moabites, who hired Balaam to curse Israel (Num. 22:2).
rendered from Hebrew words for a rod or beam of scales, a symbol of justice and fair dealing (Job 31:6; Prov. 11:1).
artificial baldness was a sign of mourning among the Jews (Isa. 22:12; Jer. 16:6) and marked the end of a Nazarite's vow; forbidden in imitation of pagan customs (Deut. 14:1).
a fragrant resin, the gum of a tree growing in Gilead (Gen. 37:25; Jer. 8:22), valued for its medicinal qualities and traded by merchants.
a height, denoting a high place where the Jews worshipped idols (Ezek. 20:29).
heights, the forty-seventh station of the Israelites in Moabite territory (Num. 21:19, 20).
heights of Baal, a place on the river Arnon east of Jordan (Josh. 13:17), perhaps the same as Bamoth.
used variously of love, unity of Christ's body the church, captivity, brotherhood, and a shepherd's staff (Hos. 11:4; Col. 3:14; Ezek. 34:27).
built, the name of several Old Testament men, including a Gadite warrior of David (2 Sam. 23:36) and a Levite prominent in post-exilic reforms (Neh. 8:7).
flags of various kinds used to mark tribal divisions on the march and as stationary signals calling people to war (Num. 2:2; Ps. 60:4).
a feast for guests (Esther 5; 1 Pet. 4:3), with customs of invitation, seating by rank, washing of hands, and honour shown by extra portions.

the ordinance instituted by Christ (Matt. 28:19-20), signifying the work of the Holy Spirit; its mode (dipping, pouring, or sprinkling) and its extension to the infant children of believers are both discussed at length by Easton.
mentioned only in 1 Cor. 15:29, possibly referring to a Corinthian custom of proxy baptism for those who died unbaptized, which Paul aimed to correct.
not Christian baptism but one binding its subjects to repentance rather than faith in Christ; those John baptized were later rebaptized by Paul (Acts 19:7).
Christ's formal inauguration into his public ministry by John, undertaken not for his own sake but as surety for his people, to "fulfil all righteousness" (Matt. 3:15).
used of the means by which a door is bolted, a rock or shore, and figuratively of fortifications or defences (Neh. 3:3; Isa. 45:2).
son of Abba, a notorious robber released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the demand of the Jews (Matt. 27:16-26).
whom God has blessed, a Buzite, father of Elihu, one of Job's friends (Job 32:2).
whom Jehovah hath blessed, father of the prophet Zechariah (Zech. 1:1; Matt. 23:35).
lightning, son of Abinoam, who at Deborah's summons defeated Jabin's army (Judg. 4); commended for his faith (Heb. 11:32).
a Greek term for one of another nation, or one not speaking Greek (Rom. 1:14; Col. 3:11; 1 Cor. 14:11).
mentioned only in Ezek. 5:1, regarding shaving the head as a sign of mourning; Nazarites were untouched by the razor.
going barefoot was a sign of great distress or calamity (Isa. 20:2-4; 2 Sam. 15:30).
fugitive, one of Shemaiah's five sons (1 Chr. 3:22).
son of Joshua, the patronymic of Elymas the sorcerer who opposed Paul and Barnabas at Paphos (Acts 13:6).
son of Jonah, the patronymic of Peter (Matt. 16:17).
painter (Ezra 2:53), father of some of the Nethinim.
a grain much cultivated in Egypt and Palestine, often food for the poor and for horses; ready for harvest by Passover time (Ruth 1:22; John 6:9).
a storehouse for grain, usually underground though sometimes above ground (Deut. 28:8; Luke 12:18).
son of consolation, surname of Joses, a Levite of Cyprus (Acts 4:36) who introduced Paul to the apostles, laboured with him at Antioch, and later separated from him over John Mark (Acts 15:36-41).
a vessel for keeping flour (1 Kings 17:12), the same word elsewhere rendered "pitcher."
barrenness was regarded as a severe reproach among the Jews (Gen. 30:1; 1 Sam. 1:6; Luke 1:25).
son of Saba, surname of Joseph (also called Justus, Acts 1:23) and of Judas the prophet (Acts 15:32).
son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3), generally identified with Nathanael.
son of Timaeus, a blind beggar of Jericho healed by Jesus for his faith (Mark 10:46).
blessed, the secretary of the prophet Jeremiah, who wrote and read his prophecies, was imprisoned with him, and probably died in Babylon (Jer. 32, 36).
of iron. A Gileadite of Rogelim distinguished for loyalty to David, providing for his followers during Absalom's revolt; David commended his children to Solomon (2 Sam. 17:27; 1 Kings 2:7).
light soil, a fertile region east of Jordan ruled by Og until defeated by Israel (Num. 21:33-35), later given to the half-tribe of Manasseh, noted for its cattle and oaks.
the Bashan of the villages of Jair, the general name given to Argob by Jair the son of Manasseh (Deut. 3:14).
(Ps. 68:15), probably another name for Hermon.
sweet-smelling. (1.) Daughter of Ishmael, one of Esau's three wives (Gen. 36:3), also called Mahalath. (2.) A daughter of Solomon (1 Kings 4:15).
the "king serpent" (Isa. 11:8), a fabulous serpent, probably referring to the yellow snake.
several Hebrew words for vessels used for washing, holding blood, or sprinkling, made of brass in the tabernacle and gold in the temple.
five different Hebrew words denote various kinds of baskets, for bread, grapes, first fruits, or figs, and Greek terms for the baskets used in the feeding miracles and Paul's escape (Acts 9:25).
in Deut. 23:2, illegitimate offspring; in Heb. 12:8, one who does not share the privileges of God's children.
beating, a common Eastern punishment referred to as "the rod of correction," limited to forty blows (Deut. 25:2-3).
a creature "flying in the dark," reckoned among unclean birds (Lev. 11:19); casting idols to bats means consigning them to desolate places (Isa. 2:20).
a Hebrew liquid measure, the tenth part of a homer, about 8 gallons 3 quarts (1 Kings 7:26).
daughter of many, one of the gates of Heshbon, near which were pools (Cant. 7:4).
the use of the bath was frequent among the Hebrews, required of the high priest at his inauguration and on the Day of Atonement (Lev. 8:6; 16:4).
daughter of the oath, daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah the Hittite; David committed adultery with her and later married her; she became mother of Solomon (2 Sam. 11-12).
a military engine consisting of a beam shaped like a ram's head, used to breach walls (Ezek. 4:2; 21:22).
a mallet or heavy war-club, applied metaphorically to Cyrus as God's instrument against Babylon (Jer. 51:20).
the war-bow used in fighting (Zech. 9:10; 10:4).
a parapet wall surrounding flat house roofs, required by law to prevent accidents (Deut. 22:8).
denotes the estuary of the Dead Sea at the Jordan's mouth (Josh. 15:5); in Zech. 6:3 it describes the strong or spirited colour of horses.
named in Ps. 37:35, probably meaning a tree "native born," growing luxuriantly in its own soil; possibly the evergreen bay laurel.
a product of the land of Havilah (Gen. 2:12), probably an aromatic gum resembling myrrh, to which manna is compared in colour (Num. 11:7).
a pole or standard set on mountain tops as a call to assemble for some national purpose (Isa. 30:17).
whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite warrior of David (1 Chr. 12:5).
citizens, a town in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:24).
rendered from various Hebrew words for a weaver's frame, crossbeam, rafter, or plank; in the New Testament contrasted with "mote" as a large versus small piece of wood (Matt. 7:3-5).
an article of diet mentioned as brought to David (2 Sam. 17:28) and used in the bread Ezekiel was commanded to make (Ezek. 4:9).
a native of Western Asian mountains; David defended his flock against one (1 Sam. 17:34-37); in Daniel's vision it represents the Medo-Persian empire (Dan. 7:5).
its care was prescribed by law (Lev. 19:27); shaving or plucking it was a sign of mourning, and cutting off another's beard a mark of indignity (2 Sam. 10:4).
used of grazing animals, beasts of burden, food animals, and figuratively of an infuriated multitude or wicked men (1 Cor. 15:32; 2 Pet. 2:12); the four beasts of Daniel 7 represent four kingdoms.
in Num. 8:4 means turned or rounded work in gold; elsewhere possibly "mixed" gold or thin gold plates.
oil obtained by pounding olives in a mortar rather than crushing them in a mill, reckoned the best (Ex. 27:20).
a gate of the temple (Acts 3:2), of massive structure covered with Corinthian brass, likely leading from the court of the Gentiles to the court of the women.
first-born, the second son of Benjamin (Gen. 46:21), whose descendants were reckoned among Ephraim.
Hebrew terms denote a simple mat, a canopied bed with curtains, or in the New Testament a litter with a coverlet (Ex. 8:3; Deut. 3:11; Mark 2:4).
one of the judges of Israel (1 Sam. 12:11), possibly a contracted form of Abdon.
an apartment furnished with an elevated platform for sleeping, used by family and guests (2 Kings 4:10).
used in Deut. 3:11, elsewhere rendered "couch" or "bed"; refers to the divan common in Eastern houses.
mentioned from Deut. 1:44; wild bees laid up honey in rocks (Ps. 81:16); Samson found a swarm in a lion's carcass (Judg. 14:8).
a name given to Satan (Matt. 10:25), probably the same as Baal-zebub, meaning "lord of flies" or "lord of dung."
well. (1.) A station of the Hebrews in the wilderness of Moab where a well was dug by Moses' direction (Num. 21:16-18). (2.) A town in Judah to which Jotham fled from Abimelech (Judg. 9:21).
well of heroes, probably the same as Beer, where the chiefs of Israel dug a well (Num. 21:16; Isa. 15:8).
illustrious. (1.) Father of Judith, one of Esau's wives (Gen. 26:34). (2.) Father of the prophet Hosea (1:1).
"the well of him that liveth and seeth me," the well where the Lord met Hagar (Gen. 16:7-14); Isaac dwelt beside it.
wells, one of the four Hivite cities that entered by fraud into a league with Joshua, belonging to Benjamin (Josh. 18:25).

entries.term: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan
entries.definition: (Deut. 10:6), the same as Bene-jaakan.

well of the oath, or of seven, dug by Abraham and renamed by Isaac after a compact with Abimelech (Gen. 21:31; 26:31-33); "from Dan to Beersheba" became a proverbial phrase for the whole Promised Land.
(Heb. hargol, "leaper"), mentioned in Lev. 11:22, denoting a winged, leaping creature akin to the locust, rendered "cricket" in the Revised Version.
an old plural of "beef," applicable to ruminating animals except camels, especially horned cattle (Lev. 22:19).
the poor were provided for under Mosaic law (Lev. 19:10), though vagrant beggars as a class are not mentioned until the New Testament (Mark 10:46).
a method of execution practised among the Egyptians and Hebrews (Gen. 40:17-19; 2 Sam. 4:8), also mentioned in the New Testament (Matt. 14:8-12).
(Job 40:15-24), probably meaning "water-ox," likely the hippopotamus.
a half shekel (Ex. 38:26), meaning a "division" or "part."
the Aramaic form of Baal, the national god of the Babylonians, meaning "lord" (Isa. 46:1).
a thing swallowed. (1.) A city near Sodom, also called Zoar, spared at Lot's intercession (Gen. 19:20-23). (2.) The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38). (3.) A king of Edom, son of Beor (Gen. 36:32).
worthlessness, used in the Old Testament as a proper name and in 2 Cor. 6:15 as a name of Satan; "son of Belial" means simply a worthless, lawless person.
small golden bells were attached to the hem of the high priest's ephod (Ex. 28:33-35); "bells of the horses" (Zech. 14:20) were attached to bridles for war horses.
mentioned only in Jer. 6:29, likely leather bags similar to those used in Egypt for casting metal.
used symbolically for carnal affections or the heart (Titus 1:12; Prov. 18:8); "belly of hell" means the grave (Jonah 2:2).
"Bel protect the king," the last king of Babylon, whose feast and doom are recorded in Dan. 5; identified in modern scholarship with the Marduk-sar-uzur of contract tablets.
"Beltis protect the king," the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).
built up by Jehovah, son of Jehoiada, chief priest, commander of David's bodyguard, later made commander-in-chief by Solomon (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 2:35).
son of my kindred, i.e., "born of incest," son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).
the deck of a Tyrian ship, overlaid with box-wood (Ezek. 27:6).
children of Jaakan (Num. 33:31-32), the same as Beeroth.
the standing title of Syrian kings meaning "son of Hadad"; several kings by this name warred against Israel and Judah (1 Kings 15:18; 2 Kings 8:7-15; 13:3-4).

son of my right hand, the younger son of Jacob by Rachel, born near Bethlehem, whose mother died naming him Ben-oni before Jacob renamed him; his tribe was famed for archers and slingers and nearly exterminated in a civil war (Judg. 20-21).
a torch. (1.) Father of Bela, a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32). (2.) Father of Balaam (Num. 22:5).
gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).
blessing. (1.) A valley near Engedi where Jehoshaphat overthrew the Moabites and Ammonites (2 Chr. 20:26). (2.) One of David's Benjamite warriors (1 Chr. 12:3).
a city of Macedonia visited by Paul, Silas, and Timothy after persecution at Thessalonica (Acts 17:10-13).
blessed by Jehovah, father of the prophet Zechariah (1:1), among several other Old Testament men of this name.
hail. (1.) A town in southern Palestine near Lahai-roi (Gen. 16:14). (2.) A grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).
a gift, or "in evil." (1.) One of Asher's sons (Gen. 46:17). (2.) A son of Ephraim, born after the slaughter of his brothers (1 Chr. 7:20-23). (3.) A Benjamite who founded Ajalon (1 Chr. 8:13).
bearer of victory, eldest daughter of Agrippa I., who lived incestuously with her brother Agrippa II. and appears with him in Acts 25-26.
the king of Babylon who sent a friendly deputation to Hezekiah (2 Kings 20:12), elsewhere called Merodach-baladan.
a precious stone, rendering of Hebrew tarshish, one of the stones on the high priest's breastplate (Ex. 28:20), possibly what is now called chrysolite.
a Hebrew word meaning "sweeper," occurs only in Isa. 14:23, of the sweeping away of Babylon.
cold, a ravine in the extreme south-west of Judah where 200 of David's men stayed behind while pursuing the Amalekites (1 Sam. 30:9-10).
occurring only in Isa. 8:21, meaning to be oppressed or in hardship.
confidence, a city belonging to Hadadezer, king of Zobah, that yielded much spoil of brass to David (2 Sam. 8:8), also called Tibhath.
occurs frequently as the appellation for "house" or "dwelling-place" in compound place names.
house of the ford, a place on the east bank of the Jordan where John was baptizing (John 1:28), possibly identical with Bethbarah.
house of response, a fenced city of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38).
house of answers, a city in the mountainous district of Judah (Josh. 15:59).

house of dates. (1.) A place east of Jordan, per the Revised Version of John 1:28. (2.) A village on the Mount of Olives, residence of Lazarus and his sisters, frequently mentioned in Christ's life (John 11:1; Mark 11:1).
house of the desert, one of the six cities of Judah in the Jordan valley (Josh. 18:22).
house of the height, a town of Gad east of Jordan opposite Jericho (Josh. 13:27), later renamed Julias or Livias by Herod.
house of God's court, a place alluded to by Hosea (10:14) as the scene of a military exploit by Shalman, probably Shalmaneser.
house of nothingness, i.e., "of idols," a place in the mountains of Benjamin east of Bethel (Josh. 7:2), used by Hosea as a contemptuous name for Bethel.
house of crossing, a ford of the Jordan south of the scene of Gideon's victory (Judg. 7:24).
sheep-house, a place to which Israel pursued the Philistines west from Mizpeh (1 Sam. 7:11).
house of Dagon, the name of two Palestinian cities, one in Judah and one near Asher (Josh. 15:41; 19:27).
house of two cakes of figs, a city of Moab denounced by Jeremiah (48:22), also called Almon-diblathaim.

house of God, a place near Jerusalem originally called Luz, site of Jacob's vision of the ladder (Gen. 28:19; 35:1-15), later one of the seats of golden-calf worship under Jeroboam, hence called Beth-aven by Hosea in contempt.
a designation of Hiel, who rebuilt Jericho under the curse pronounced by Joshua (1 Kings 16:34).
dissection or separation, mountains mentioned in Cant. 2:17, probably near Lebanon.
house of mercy, a reservoir with five porches near the sheep-gate in Jerusalem where the infirm waited for the troubling of the water (John 5:2); its exact site remains uncertain.
camel-house, a city in the plain country of Moab denounced by Jeremiah (48:23).
house of Gilgal, a place from which people gathered to celebrate the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls (Neh. 12:29).
house of a vineyard, a place in Judah where a war beacon was to be set up against the Babylonians (Jer. 6:1).
house of the hollow, the name of two towns in Ephraim, "the upper" and "the nether," the scene of Joshua's victory over the five Amorite kings (Josh. 10:10-11).
house of wastes, a town near Abel-shittim east of Jordan where Israel encamped before crossing (Num. 33:49).
house of dust (Micah 1:10), probably a town in the Shephelah between Joppa and Gaza.

house of bread. (1.) A city in the hill country of Judah, originally Ephrath, birthplace of David and of Christ, scene of Herod's slaughter of the innocents (Gen. 35:19; Matt. 2:6, 16). (2.) A city of Zebulun (Josh. 19:15).
house of Peor, a place in Moab near which Moses was probably buried (Deut. 3:29; 34:6).
house of the unripe fig, a village on the Mount of Olives near Bethany, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho (Matt. 21:1).

house of fish. (1.) A town in Galilee, native place of Peter, Andrew, and Philip (John 1:44). (2.) A city near which Christ fed 5,000, east of the lake, enlarged by Philip the tetrarch as "Julias" (Luke 9:10).
house of security, a city belonging to Manasseh where the bodies of Saul and his sons were fastened to the walls (1 Chr. 7:29; 1 Sam. 31:10), later called Scythopolis.
house of the sun, the name of several cities, notably a sacerdotal city of Dan on Judah's border, scene of a battle between Jehoash and Amaziah (2 Kings 14:11-13).
house of apples, a town of Judah, now Tuffuh, near Hebron (Josh. 15:53).
man of God. (1.) Son of Nahor by Milcah, father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:22-23). (2.) A southern city of Judah (1 Chr. 4:30).
house of rock, a town in the mountains of Judah built by Rehoboam for defence (2 Chr. 11:7).
to promise "by one's truth"; from betrothal, a woman was regarded as the lawful wife of the man to whom she was engaged (Deut. 28:30; Matt. 1:18-21).
married, used metaphorically in Isa. 62:4 as a name for Judea, signifying it was favoured and blessed of the Lord.
to reveal or disclose, an old English word equivalent to "betray" (Prov. 27:16; Matt. 26:73).
used with reference to Jordan, meaning the west side in the writings of Moses and the east side in the writings of Joshua, depending on the writer's location.
"in the shadow of God," the chief artificer of the tabernacle's metal, wood, and stone work, of the tribe of Judah (Ex. 31:2; 35:30).
lightning. (1.) The residence of Adoni-bezek in Judah (Judg. 1:5). (2.) The place where Saul numbered the forces of Israel and Judah (1 Sam. 11:8).
ore of gold or silver. (1.) A city of the Reubenites, one of three cities of refuge east of Jordan (Josh. 20:8). (2.) A descendant of Asher (1 Chr. 7:37).

the English form of the Greek Biblia, "books," the collection of sixty-six sacred books composed by many writers over about 1600 years, divided into the Old Testament (thirty-nine books) and New Testament (twenty-seven books).
the frame on which dead bodies were conveyed to the grave (Luke 7:14).
garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs of Ahasuerus's harem (Esther 1:10).
one of the eunuchs who conspired against Ahasuerus's life, detected by Mordecai and hanged (Esther 2:21-23).
son of contention, "the Shuhite," one of Job's three friends who spoke against him in stern, severe tones (Job 8, 18, 25).
cheerful. (1.) Head of the fifteenth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:14). (2.) A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:5).
faltering, Rachel's handmaid given to Jacob, mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 29:29; 30:3-8); Reuben was cursed for committing adultery with her.
son of the tongue, i.e., "eloquent," a man who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2).
divided under the Mosaic law into clean and unclean species (Lev. 11:13-20); birds offered in sacrifice were not divided as other victims were (Gen. 15:10).
son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah succoured by Abraham in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).
a newborn child was washed, rubbed with salt, and swathed (Ezek. 16:4); a mother remained in seclusion forty or eighty days before offering a purification sacrifice (Lev. 12:1-8).
the observance of birthdays was common in early times, especially in Egypt (Gen. 40:20); John the Baptist was beheaded on Herod's birthday (Matt. 14:6).
special privileges of the first-born son, including priesthood of the family and a double portion of inheritance, which could be forfeited or transferred (Gen. 25:33; 49:4; Deut. 21:15-17).
an overseer; in apostolic times there was no distinction of order between bishops and elders/presbyters, the terms designating the same office (Acts 20:17-28; Phil. 1:1).
the curb placed in horses' mouths to restrain them, generally made of bronze or iron (Ps. 32:9; James 3:3).
the broken or divided place, a district in the Jordan valley east of the river (2 Sam. 2:29).
a province in Asia Minor south of the Euxine where early Christian congregations formed (1 Pet. 1:1); Paul was prevented by the Spirit from entering it (Acts 16:7).
symbolic of affliction, misery, and servitude (Ex. 1:14; Ruth 1:20); the Passover was eaten with bitter herbs representing the harshness of Egyptian bondage.
mentioned in connection with the desolation of Babylon, Idumea, and Nineveh (Isa. 14:23), a solitary marsh-dwelling bird, though the Hebrew word is rendered "porcupine" in the Revised Version.
(Gen. 11:3), a mineral pitch, rendered "slime" in the Authorized Version, used to seal Noah's ark and the ark of bulrushes (Ex. 2:3).
properly the absence of colour; in Prov. 7:9 the Hebrew word means "the pupil of the eye," elsewhere the ordinary colour term (Lev. 13:31; Cant. 1:5).
applied to the point of a spear or sword, the blade of a dagger, the "shoulder blade," or the blade of grain (Job 39:23; Matt. 13:26).
occurs only with the sixth plague of Egypt (Ex. 9:9-10), called "the botch of Egypt," likely a form of black leprosy producing burning ulcers.

speaking evil of God (Ps. 74:18) or any kind of calumny or abuse; Christ was accused of blasphemy for claiming to be the Son of God (Matt. 26:65); blasphemy against the Holy Ghost is regarded as continued, obstinate rejection of the gospel (Matt. 12:31-32).
chamberlain to King Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20).
imperfection or bodily deformity excluding men from the priesthood and animals from sacrifice (Lev. 21:17-23); the church is described as "without blemish" in Christ (Eph. 5:27).
God blesses his people with gifts; people bless God in thanksgiving, bless themselves in invoking God's favour, and bless one another in prayer or good wishes (Gen. 1:22; Ps. 103:1; Gen. 24:60).
blind beggars are frequently mentioned (Matt. 9:27); blindness was sometimes a punishment (1 Sam. 11:2) and figuratively denotes ignorance of spiritual things (Isa. 6:10).

prohibited as food (Gen. 9:4; Acts 15:29); sacrificial blood was sprinkled on the altar and people to consecrate a covenant (Ex. 24:8); human bloodshed required avenging by the nearest relative (Num. 35:24, 27).
the sign of our Lord's agony in Gethsemane (Luke 22:44).
a stain or reproach (Job 31:7); to blot out sin is to forgive it (Ps. 51:1, 9).
a colour generally associated with purple, used for the high priest's ephod and various sacred cloths (Ex. 25:4; 28:31).
sons of thunder, a surname given by Christ to James and John for their fervid, impetuous temper (Mark 3:17).
occurs only in Ps. 80:13, the same Hebrew word elsewhere rendered "swine," an animal the Hebrews abhorred as food.
alacrity. (1.) The wealthy Bethlehemite who married Ruth under the levirate law (Ruth 4:1-13). (2.) The name of one of two brazen pillars Solomon set up in the temple court (1 Kings 7:21).
weepers, a place where the angel of the Lord reproved Israel for making a league with the Canaanites, causing them bitterly to weep (Judg. 2:1, 5).
an aggravated ulcer, as in the case of Hezekiah (2 Kings 20:7) or the Egyptians (Ex. 9:9-11), also the disease of Job, probably black leprosy.
(Ex. 9:31), meaning "swollen or podded for seed," or as the Revised Version has it, "was in bloom."
a Hebrew term for a counterpane, cushion, or the place "at his head" where a sleeper rested (1 Sam. 19:13; 26:7).
an obligation of any kind (Num. 30:2); Christian love is called "the bond of perfectness" (Col. 3:14).
used of Israel's slavery in Egypt, "the house of bondage" (Ex. 13:3), and later of the Babylonian captivity.
a turban worn by priests, or a head-dress worn by women, consisting of a piece of cloth twisted about the head (Ex. 39:28; Isa. 3:20).

rendered from Hebrew sepher, "a writing" or "roll"; ancient books were written on skins, cloth, or papyrus and rolled up like scrolls; "the book of life" symbolizes the roll of citizens of God's kingdom (Ps. 69:28; Rev. 20:15).
a hut of branches, such as Jacob made at Succoth (Gen. 33:17) and Israelites erected at the Feast of Tabernacles (Lev. 23:42-43).
captives, cattle, or valuables taken in war, whose division was regulated by law (Num. 31:26-47); David introduced sharing the booty equally with the baggage-guard (1 Sam. 30:24-26).
the Israelites "borrowed" from the Egyptians at the Exodus (Ex. 12:35), though the Hebrew word properly means to "ask" or "request," not to borrow with intent to return.
carrying objects in the bosom denotes kindness, secrecy, or intimacy (Gen. 16:5); Christ is said to be "in the bosom of the Father" (John 1:18), signifying perfect intimacy.
the Chaldee form of the name Beor, father of Balaam (2 Pet. 2:15).
the projecting, convex parts of a shield (Job 15:26).
the name given in Deut. 28:27 to one of the Egyptian plagues, usually rendered "boil."
a skin vessel for holding wine, milk, or water (Josh. 9:4; Judg. 4:19); earthenware bottles were also used, and the "bottles of heaven" figuratively denote the clouds (Job 38:37).

used in war and hunting from earliest times (Gen. 21:20); the tribe of Benjamin was famous for archery; the bow is a symbol of victory and, when broken or deceitful, of falsehood (Ps. 7:12; Hos. 7:16).
compassionate feelings (Phil. 1:8), rendered "tender mercies" in the Revised Version.
a common gesture of respect or adoration, to men, idols, or God (Gen. 23:7; Josh. 5:14).
the sockets of the golden candlestick's lamps are called bowls, the same word elsewhere rendered "cup" (Ex. 25:31).
a small vessel for holding oil or perfume, more properly rendered "vial" (Mark 14:3; 1 Sam. 10:1).
(Heb. teashshur), a species of tree mentioned in Isa. 60:13, identified as the Buxus sempervirens, noted for its hard, durable wood.
enclosure; fortress. (1.) The city of Jobab, an early Edomite king (Gen. 36:33). (2.) A Moabite city in the plain country (Jer. 48:24).
ornaments worn on the wrist or ankle by both men and women, of various Hebrew terms and forms (Gen. 24:22; Cant. 5:14).
rendered from two Hebrew words for thorny shrubs common in Palestine, resembling the hawthorn or common thistle (Judg. 9:14; Isa. 34:13).
a symbol of kings descended from royal ancestors, of prosperity, and especially of the Messiah, "the Branch" springing from the root of Jesse (Isa. 11:1; Jer. 23:5; Zech. 3:8).

properly copper, used for fetters, armour, musical instruments, and money; a symbol of insensibility in sin and of strength; the brazen serpent Moses made was later destroyed by Hezekiah for becoming an object of superstition (Num. 21:4-9; 2 Kings 18:4).
(Isa. 3:18), an old English word meaning comeliness or beauty.
an opening in a wall, the fracture of a limb, or figuratively a bay or harbour (1 Kings 11:27; Lev. 24:20).
generally made of wheat, kneaded and baked as thin cakes, often in public ovens; unleavened at Passover; the twelve loaves of showbread represented the twelve tribes (Ex. 29:2; 25:30).

(1.) Armour protecting the breast, used figuratively in Eph. 6:14. (2.) An ornament on the high priest's breast set with twelve precious stones bearing the tribal names, called "the breastplate of judgment" (Ex. 28:15-29).
linen drawers worn by priests, reaching from the waist above the knee (Ex. 28:42).
forbidden under the law, "for the gift maketh open eyes blind" (Ex. 23:8).
the chief labour of the Israelites in Egypt (Ex. 1:13-14), usually dried in the sun though sometimes kiln-fired; the tower of Babel used burnt bricks cemented with bitumen (Gen. 11:3).
used in the ordinary sense and figuratively of the church's relation to Christ, "the Bridegroom" (John 3:29; Rev. 21:9).
three Hebrew words denote a muzzle, bit, or halter-rein by which a rider controls a horse, used figuratively of divine restraint (Ps. 32:9; Isa. 37:29).
several Hebrew terms for thorny shrubs used for hedges or growing wild, sometimes symbolizing troublesome men (Micah 7:4; Isa. 10:17).
(Jer. 46:4), an obsolete term for a scale coat of armour, rendered "coat of mail" in the Revised Version.
an inflammable mineral found near the Dead Sea, associated with the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and figuratively of punishment (Gen. 19:24; Rev. 14:10).
a torrent, applied to small streams, winter torrents, or their beds, and in Isa. 19:7 to the river Nile.

used variously of natural siblings, near relations, fellow-countrymen, disciples, fellow believers, colleagues, and fellow men (Matt. 1:2; Gen. 13:8; Acts 9:30); the "brethren of Jesus" were probably the younger children of Joseph and Mary.
a rumour or report (Jer. 10:22; Nah. 3:19).
a vessel for drawing water, used figuratively of a numerous issue (Num. 24:7).
a portable or full-body shield, sometimes a lance improperly translated "buckler"; shields taken from enemies were kept as mementoes in the temple (2 Sam. 22:31; 2 Kings 11:10).
Jewish architecture adopted Canaanite styles, with Phoenician assistance in constructing the temple and palace; believers are called "God's building" (1 Cor. 3:9).
rainy, the eighth ecclesiastical month, later called Marchesvan (1 Kings 6:38).
a generic term for horned cattle or an animal of the ox kind used in sacrifice, sometimes rendered "cow," "ox," or "calf" (Isa. 65:25; Lev. 9:3).
the Egyptian papyrus plant, used for garments, ropes, and paper, and for the ark in which Moses was placed (Ex. 2:3).
mural towers or bastions, introduced by King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:15).
used of a bundle of twigs, a cake of raisins, or the hump of a camel (Ex. 12:22; 2 Sam. 16:1; Isa. 30:6).
a load, a severe task, a difficult duty, or a prophecy of calamity (Ex. 23:5; Isa. 13:1).

patriarchal and later Hebrew burial customs, from Abraham's purchase of the cave of Machpelah for Sarah to the burial of kings "in the city of David" and Christ's burial in a new rock-hewn tomb (Gen. 23; Matt. 27:57-60).
Hebrew olah, "ascending," a sacrifice wholly consumed by fire, the most frequent form of offering from Abel onward, later regulated in detail by the law of Moses (Gen. 4:4; Lev. 1).
the plant, probably a mimosa or acacia, in which Jehovah appeared to Moses (Ex. 3:2).
a servant in charge of the wine, such as Pharaoh's cupbearer and Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes (Gen. 40:1-13; Neh. 1:11).
curdled milk or a semi-fluid cream, distinguished from modern churned butter (Gen. 18:8; Job 20:17).
contempt. (1.) The second son of Nahor, ancestor of Elihu (Gen. 22:21). (2.) A chief of Gad (1 Chr. 5:14). (3.) A district in Arabia (Jer. 25:23).
the father of the prophet Ezekiel (1:3).
in "by myself" (1 Cor. 4:4), meaning "against myself" per the Revised Version.
immediately (Matt. 13:21).
winding or twisted roads (Judg. 5:6; Ps. 125:5).
an object of talk, taunt, or derision, rendered from several Hebrew terms (Job 30:9; Deut. 28:37).
a dry measure, the sixth part of a seah, equal to about two English quarts (2 Kings 6:25).
arched vaults or recesses off a passage, cells for closer confinement of prisoners (Jer. 37:16).

(1.) A town on the eastern border of Asher (Josh. 19:27). (2.) A district of twenty cities given by Solomon to Hiram, who was displeased with the gift and gave the district the name meaning "good for nothing" (1 Kings 9:13).
the title assumed by Roman emperors after Julius Caesar, given in the New Testament to various emperors as sovereigns of Judea, including Augustus, Tiberius, Claudius, and Nero.

a city near the source of the Jordan at the base of Mount Hermon, originally a Canaanite sanctuary of Baal, later enlarged by Herod Philip and named for himself and Augustus; the northern limit of Christ's public ministry (Matt. 16:13).

a city on the Mediterranean coast built by Herod the Great and named for Augustus, capital of Roman Judea and seat of its governors; Cornelius was converted here (Acts 10), and Paul was imprisoned here for two years.
a basket of wicker-work for holding captured birds (Jer. 5:27; Amos 8:1); in Rev. 18:2 rendered from a Greek word for prison.

the Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) during Christ's ministry and at his trial, who advised that Jesus should die "for the people" (John 11:50), sending him to Pilate since he lacked power to inflict death.

(1.) The first-born son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground, who murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy over God's acceptance of Abel's offering, and was expelled from Eden as a marked wanderer (Gen. 4). (2.) A town of the Kenites near Engedi (Josh. 15:57).
(1.) The fourth antediluvian patriarch, son of Enos, who lived 910 years (Gen. 5:9-14). (2.) The son of Arphaxad, named in Luke 3:36 but not in the Old Testament.
wheat or barley bread offered in the temple, salted but unleavened; various kinds are described in Lev. 2, including honey-cakes and fig-cakes.
one of the most ancient cities of Assyria, founded by Nimrod (Gen. 10:11), later capital of the empire, identified with the Nimrud ruins.
an aromatic reed, one of the ingredients of the holy anointing oil (Ex. 30:23), imported from Arabia or India, also called "sweet cane."
one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom (1 Kings 4:31).

a dog. Several Old Testament men of this name; most notably the son of Jephunneh, one of the twelve spies sent to Canaan, who alone with Joshua encouraged the people and was spared the wilderness plague, later receiving Hebron as his inheritance (Num. 13-14; Josh. 14).

commonly used in sacrifice; the golden calf Aaron made was likely modeled on Moloch rather than the Egyptian Apis; Jeroboam later set up two golden calves at Dan and Bethel to keep Israel from worshipping in Jerusalem (Ex. 32:4; 1 Kings 12:28).
workmen who stopped the seams of ships' decks and sides, employed by Tyre (Ezek. 27:9, 27).
used of crying to God in prayer, and of God's calling men to office or to accept his grace; an "effectual call" is the internal work of the Holy Spirit enabling belief (John 6:44-45).
a profession or vocation (1 Cor. 7:20); "the hope of your calling" (Eph. 4:4) is the hope from being called into God's kingdom.
one of the four cities founded by Nimrod (Gen. 10:10), a trading partner of Tyre, later destroyed by Assyria; also called Calno and Canneh.
the Latin name for the place of the skull where Christ was crucified, outside the city walls, likely named for its skull-like shape (Luke 23:33).

a beast of burden and riding from earliest times, unclean as food, used in war and commerce; John the Baptist wore raiment of camel's hair; proverbially it is "easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye" than for a rich man to enter the kingdom (Matt. 19:24).
the place where Jair the judge was buried (Judg. 10:5), probably the modern Tell-el-Kaimun on the slopes of Carmel.
the Israelite tribes formed structured encampments during their wilderness journey, arranged around the tabernacle (Num. 2); after entering Canaan, "camp" referred exclusively to war camps.
the henna plant (Cant. 1:14), producing flowers from which Eastern women made an auburn dye for their nails and hands, found at Engedi.
a town of Galilee near Capernaum where Christ turned water into wine, his first miracle (John 2:1-11), and the birthplace of Nathanael.

(1.) The fourth son of Ham, cursed for his father's transgression, ancestor of eleven tribes (Gen. 9-10). (2.) The land west of the Jordan named for him, meaning "the lowlands," whose extent is described throughout the Pentateuch.
a name given to the apostle Simon (Matt. 10:4), a transliteration of an Aramaic word for the Zealot sect, not indicating descent from Canaan.

descendants of Canaan who spread across Palestine and beyond, famous as merchants and seamen worshipping Baal, whom Israel was commanded to destroy upon entering the Promised Land but never fully dispossessed.
(Isa. 19:18) the language spoken by Jews in Palestine, essentially the same as Phoenician and closely related to Hebrew.
the queen of the Ethiopians whose treasurer was converted by Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27); "Candace" was a title common to several successive queens.
Hebrew ner, properly "lamp," used figuratively of conscience, Christian example, and prosperity (Prov. 20:27; Matt. 5:14-15).

the golden lamp-stand Moses was commanded to make for the tabernacle (Ex. 25:31-40), lighted nightly to provide light in the windowless tent and symbolizing the church as light of the world; Solomon's temple had ten, the post-exilic temple one, later carried to Rome by Titus.
a tall sedgy reed plant (Isa. 43:24), used figuratively of weak, fragile things.
a spreading gangrene (2 Tim. 2:17); in James 5:3 "cankered" means rusted or tarnished.
"the licking locust" that consumes grass, probably a stage of the locust's growth (Joel 1:4).
mentioned only in Ezek. 27:23, likely the same as Calneh.
the authoritative collection of inspired Scripture, the Old Testament closed probably by the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, the New Testament substantially fixed by the middle of the second century.
a Galilean city on the Sea of Galilee that became Christ's "own city" after his rejection at Nazareth, the scene of many miracles, denounced for its unbelief (Matt. 11:23), identified with Tell Hum.
the original home of the Philistines (Deut. 2:23), possibly Crete or a part of the Nile Delta.
the largest eastern province of Asia Minor, where Christianity spread early; Cappadocians were present at Pentecost (Acts 2:9).
several Hebrew and Greek words denote military, civil, and honorary leaders; Christ is called "the Captain of our salvation" (Heb. 2:10) as author and head of his people's deliverance.
one taken in war, often treated with great cruelty; conquered cities' men were slain and women and children carried away as slaves.

the successive Assyrian deportations of the ten tribes of Israel (culminating 721 B.C.) and the Babylonian deportations of Judah under Nebuchadnezzar (culminating in the destruction of Jerusalem, 586 B.C.), ended by Cyrus's decree permitting return in 536 B.C.
a red gem in the high priest's breastplate, from a root meaning "to glitter" (Ex. 28:17), possibly the garnet.
contact with a dead body made an Israelite ceremonially unclean under Mosaic law (Num. 19:16).
"fortress of Chemosh," a city on the Euphrates, capital of the northern Hittite kingdom, where Nebuchadnezzar defeated Pharaoh-necho (B.C. 607).
a park. (1.) A prominent wooded headland of Central Palestine where Elijah defeated the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18). (2.) A town in the hill country of Judah, home of Nabal and Abigail (1 Sam. 25).
vine-dresser, the name of several Old Testament men, including the father of Achan, "the troubler of Israel" (Josh. 7:1).
used of the unconverted mind at enmity with God (Rom. 8:6-7), of fleshly enjoyments, and of the outward, bodily rites of the Mosaic ceremonial law.
an artificer in stone, iron, and copper as well as wood; Christ was called "the carpenter's son" and "the carpenter" (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).
rendered from several Hebrew words meaning valuables, baggage, or equipment carried by travellers (Judg. 18:21; Acts 21:15).
a wheeled vehicle usually drawn by oxen, used to transport the ark and its utensils (1 Sam. 6:7; Num. 7:3).
engraving and carving were practised in constructing the tabernacle and temple and ornamenting priestly dress; Isaiah describes the carving of wooden idols (Isa. 44:13-17).
an open-work barrier before windows, admitting cool air (Prov. 7:6).
a place between Babylon and Jerusalem where Iddo resided (Ezra 8:17).
a people descended from Mizraim, probably settled in Lower Egypt (Gen. 10:14).
an aromatic spice from the inner bark of a cinnamon-like tree, one ingredient of the holy anointing oil (Ex. 30:24).
one regarded as unworthy or rejected, used by Paul of himself if disqualified through lack of self-discipline (1 Cor. 9:27).
a military fortress or watch-tower; the "castle" of Acts 21:34 was the Roman garrison quarters in the fortress of Antonia at Jerusalem.
the "Dioscuri," twin heroes of Greek mythology regarded as patrons of sailors, whose figures were on the prow of the ship Paul sailed in (Acts 28:11).
"the consumer," probably a species or growth-stage of the locust (1 Kings 8:37).
the epistles of James, Peter, John, and Jude, so called because addressed to Christians generally rather than to a specific church.
the chief occupation of the inhabitants of Palestine; classified as neat cattle (oxen) and small cattle (sheep and goats), central to sacrifice, food, and wealth.
the membrane covering the upper part of the liver, offered in sacrifice (Ex. 29:13); a different word denotes the pericardium in Hos. 13:8.
ornamental network caps for containing women's hair (Isa. 3:18).
a raised way or ascent between Zion and the temple (1 Chr. 26:16).
numerous natural caves in Palestine's limestone rocks served as burial places (the cave of Machpelah), refuges (Adullam, Engedi), and dwellings.
a stately, durable, fragrant tree, abundant on Lebanon, used extensively in Solomon's temple and palace and often used figuratively of might and majesty (Isa. 2:13).
"the black torrent," the brook flowing through the ravine below Jerusalem's eastern wall (John 18:1); also spelled Kidron.
the covering of a house's inside roof and walls with wood planks, sometimes adorned with stucco, gold, or ivory (1 Kings 6:9).
a subterranean vault or storehouse, also used for the temple or royal treasury (1 Chr. 27:28).
the eastern harbour of Corinth, from which Paul sailed on his return from his second missionary journey, and where a church existed (Acts 18:18; Rom. 16:1).
a vessel for burning incense before the Lord, of brass for daily use and gold for the Day of Atonement (Lev. 16:12).
five recorded censuses of Israel are noted in Scripture, from the Exodus (603,550 men) through the post-exilic count (42,360), plus one under Roman rule in Christ's time (Luke 2:1).
a Roman officer commanding a hundred men; several centurions in the New Testament, including Cornelius and the one who watched Christ's crucifixion, are spoken of favourably.
a Syriac surname meaning "rock" given by Christ to Simon (John 1:42), translated Petros/Peter in Greek.
see Caesarea.
the refuse of winnowed grain, usually burned, used figuratively of the wicked's powerlessness and destruction (Ps. 1:4; Matt. 3:12).
used as insignia of office (Gen. 41:42), as ornament, and as fetters for prisoners, sometimes attaching a captive to a soldier as with Paul and Peter.
a precious stone in the foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev. 21:19), likely the Hebrew nophekh elsewhere translated "emerald."
the southern portion of Babylonia along the Euphrates, homeland of Abraham's ancestor Ur, whose ancient history has been illuminated by archaeological discoveries.
the Aramaic dialect used in portions of Daniel and Ezra, the common language of commerce that gradually became the popular speech of post-exilic Palestine.
the Chaldeans, inhabitants of Babylon's territory, later a learned class of astrologers and magi under the Babylonian empire.
an upper or inner room, sometimes used for prayer or private lodging; "chambers of imagery" (Ezek. 8:12) refers to idolatrous images the prophet saw in vision.
wantonness or impurity (Rom. 13:13).
a confidential royal servant or eunuch; Erastus "the chamberlain" of Rom. 16:23 was the city treasurer of Corinth.
